metadata.title: Results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024: Strengthening early childhood education and care, TALIS, OECD Publishing, Paris

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Spain participant note reports descriptive survey results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024, based on self-reports from ECEC staff and setting leaders in pre-primary settings (ISCED 02). The note describes the survey’s aim to obtain representative samples within each participating country or subnational entity, but it does not specify the technical weighting variables (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures. Because the document is a participant results note rather than an analysis paper estimating model-based effects, it does not provide guidance on which weight variables analysts should apply in microdata analyses. For any secondary analysis using the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database, analysts should follow the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 technical documentation for complex survey design and apply the provided sampling/replicate weights to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this participant note does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with PV-based scaling; it reports questionnaire-based indicators (e.g., percentages of staff/leaders reporting practices, needs, stress, and intentions). Missing-data handling is not reported because the note is a descriptive results summary and does not document any imputation or deletion strategy for item nonresponse. This omission is therefore a reporting gap for secondary analysts, but it is consistent with the document’s purpose as a high-level results note rather than a methodological analysis paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note focuses on Spain’s TALIS Starting Strong 2024 pre-primary settings (Education Infantil – Segundo ciclo) for children aged 3–6 (ISCED 02). It reports indicators derived from staff and setting leader questionnaires for the participating ECEC settings in Spain; no further inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., specific item-completion thresholds or missing-data exclusions) are provided in the excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is an OECD large-scale survey of early childhood education and care (ECEC) staff and setting leaders, using questionnaires to capture staff/leader background, training, daily work, practices with children and families, and well-being and career intentions. In this Spain participant note, the focus is on pre-primary settings (ISCED 02; Education Infantil – Segundo ciclo) serving children aged 3–6, and the reported indicators are descriptive percentages (e.g., educational attainment, time allocation, professional development needs, family engagement practices, stress sources, and workforce retention intentions). The note compares Spain’s results with other participating countries and subnational entities and highlights system-level patterns such as high educational attainment, comparatively high planning time, and stress linked to administrative workload and documentation. The document does not present student-level predictive modeling, plausible-value scaling, or model performance metrics; therefore, it should be interpreted as descriptive evidence for policy discussion rather than causal inference. The note also flags that estimates should be interpreted with caution due to higher risk of non-response bias.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a participant results note summarizing descriptive survey indicators rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, it does not report an analytic sample size, PV handling, missing-data strategy, or any machine-learning model specifications or performance metrics. The extraction therefore leaves ML- and model-specific fields empty by design, while still capturing the survey scope (TALIS Starting Strong 2024, Spain, ISCED 02 pre-primary) and the key descriptive outcomes reported.
